name: Tokyo Electron Limited
blurb: Tokyo Electron (TEL) is Japan's largest semiconductor equipment company and the world's third-largest overall, behind Applied Materials and Lam Research. TEL specialises in thermal processing, deposition (CVD/ALD), coater/developer systems, and plasma etch tools. Its coater/developer systems hold a near-monopoly position in the photolithography track — the equipment that applies and develops photoresist before and after EUV or DUV exposure. Every wafer made at TSMC, Samsung, or Intel's leading-edge fabs uses TEL track systems. TEL is also a major supplier to Chinese fabs under applicable export-control constraints.
recent: TEL has benefited from the sustained semiconductor equipment investment cycle. Forward P/E of ~30.9x on 17.8% EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.74 — somewhat premium to the equipment peer group. The company is navigating U.S. export-control restrictions on advanced tools shipped to China while managing strong demand from non-China advanced logic and memory customers. TEL's high exposure to the Japanese yen creates currency headwinds when the yen appreciates.
